- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak values by 2–5% relative to sentiment-driven highs.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.3) — increase forecast lows by 2–5% to compensate for sentiment-driven weakness.
- Avoid overreacting to recent spikes — if sentiment is high but price just spiked, cap forecast rise at 3–4% above prior peak to prevent overshoot.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is rising, reduce forecast tail (last 5 days) by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence in long-term trend.
- Lag correction: if forecast is >10% above true outcome at day 1–3, reduce subsequent days’ forecast by 0.5–1% to account for delayed reaction.
